newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA kidnap victim shot, gravely wounded in Spain.
newsitem.headline: ETA kidnap victim shot, gravely wounded in Spain.

text.p: A Spanish politician kidnapped by Basque ETA guerrillas was found shot in the head on Saturday and is in "extremely serious" condition, hospital officials said.
They said he was in a coma with a bullet lodged in his brain and surgeons were operating.
Basque guerrillas ETA kidnapped Miguel Angel Blanco on Thursday and threatened to kill him at 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Saturday if the government did not change its prison policy.
Blanco had been found, with his hands tied, by a hunter who heard a shot in a wooded area near the northern Basque coastal city of San Sebastian. He was rushed to hospital.
Officials said at first that he was dead.
The attempted killing took place despite a rally of half a million Spaniards led by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar in the Basque capital Bilbao on Saturday to protest against the kidnapping.

Residents in Ermua, Blanco's hometown, and thousands of supporters at a vigil that started as ETA's deadline passed, began screaming and crying when the erroneous news that he had been killed was announced.
Hundreds then headed toward the offices of ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna yelling "assassins" and "sons of bitches".
The crowd relaxed with the news that Blanco was alive. The village resumed the vigil, awaiting news of his condition.
The government called for calm in the region.
"I want to make a first call for calm in these very bad times for Basque society, for Spain and for the family of Miguel Angel Blanco," government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told state radio.

ETA has killed some 800 people since starting a drive for Basque independence in 1968. The rebels have set deadlines to execute kidnap victims twice before, in 1981 and 1983, and in both cases the hostages were killed.
